review: Drafted by OpenRouter free models, then reviewed in a second pass by an AI (Claude, from memory) that dropped venues it could not vouch for and corrected known errors. Not independently sourced, so check anything you rely on. Positions inside a city (Atlantic City, Biloxi, Hot Springs) are illustrative.

casinos.name: Saratoga Race Course

mob.summary: Legally chartered thoroughbred track; no documented mob control.

events.text: First meet held; oldest major U.S. track.
Survived statewide betting ban via pari-mutuel.
Continues annual summer meet.

casinos.blurb: Historic thoroughbred track operating continuously since 1863, anchor of legal gambling in Saratoga.

casinos.name: Canfield Casino

mob.summary: A 19th-century gambling house; its later era (Richard Canfield) predates organised crime as the 20th century knew it.

events.text: Opened by John Morrissey in Congress Park.
Closed by state anti-gambling law.
Restored as museum.

casinos.blurb: Gilded Age casino founded by prizefighter John Morrissey, legal until New York banned gambling in 1907.

casinos.name: The Arlington Hotel

mob.summary: Owney Madden and later Benny Binion held interests; Kefauver Committee 1950 named it a mob-controlled casino.

events.text: Original hotel opened as luxury resort.
Rebuilt after fire; casino expanded in basement.
Cited in Kefauver Committee hearings as mob-operated.
Gambling shut down by Gov. Orval Faubus.

casinos.blurb: Historic bathhouse-row resort whose basement casino was a centerpiece of Hot Springs' wide-open era until 1964.

casinos.name: The Ohio Club

mob.summary: Longstanding bar with back-room gambling; machine protection alleged but no federal convictions.

events.text: Opened as saloon; gambling added later.
Gambling ended with statewide closure order.

casinos.blurb: Arkansas' oldest bar, operating back-room games under political protection until 1964.

casinos.name: The Southern Club

mob.summary: Run by Leo McLaughlin's political machine with Chicago Outfit backing; raids documented in 1960s.

events.text: Opened as private club with gambling upstairs.
Federal raid seized slot machines and records.
Closed permanently after state crackdown.

casinos.blurb: Flagship illegal club on Central Avenue, emblematic of the city's machine-protected gambling.

casinos.name: The Vapors Club

mob.summary: Owned by Owney Madden associate; listed in Kefauver Committee exhibits as mob revenue source.

events.text: Opened near the Arlington Hotel.
Named in Kefauver Committee report.
Shut down by Arkansas State Police.

casinos.blurb: High-profile nightclub and casino backed by Chicago Outfit interests during the city's peak gambling years.

casinos.name: Four Deuces

mob.summary: Al Capone's Prohibition-era headquarters, with a speakeasy, brothel and gambling above 2222 South Wabash.

events.text: Opened as Capone's headquarters and gambling den.
Raided and closed by authorities.

casinos.blurb: Al Capone's infamous South Side club that served as Outfit headquarters and illegal casino.

casinos.name: Cal Neva Lodge

mob.summary: Frank Sinatra's 1960s ownership partnered with Sam Giancana; FBI surveillance documented Outfit use of the property.

events.text: Original lodge opens on the California-Nevada state line.
Frank Sinatra buys property; Sam Giancana becomes hidden partner per FBI files.
Closes for renovation; remains shuttered as of 2024.

casinos.blurb: Historic cross-state resort infamous for Sinatra-Giancana partnership and documented Chicago Outfit infiltration.

casinos.name: Lookout House

mob.summary: Cleveland mob partners ran gaming; Kefauver Committee and FBI surveillance confirmed.

events.text: Opened as roadhouse with gambling.
Cited in Kefauver Committee report.
Demolished after gambling ended.

casinos.blurb: Covington's premier mob-backed casino, operating openly for decades across from Cincinnati.

casinos.name: Grand Terrace Cafe

mob.summary: The jazz club was controlled by Capone associates; owner Ed Fox answered to the Outfit.

events.text: Opened as a cafe and ballroom with gambling.
Closed after federal pressure.

casinos.blurb: A Bronzeville landmark where the Outfit ran high-stakes gambling above a popular dance hall.

casinos.name: Bill Miller's Riviera Casino

mob.summary: Fort Lee clubs of the 1930s-50s were reported to pay protection and share profits with New York mob figures.

events.text: Opened as high-end illegal casino on Palisades cliffs by Bill Miller.
Kefauver Committee hears testimony identifying Riviera as Chicago Outfit/Genovese operation.
Raided and closed by NJ State Police after gubernatorial pressure.

casinos.blurb: Premier illegal Bergen County casino 1930-53, documented Chicago Outfit and Genovese family operation per Kefauver Committee.

casinos.name: Glenn Rendezvous

mob.summary: Operated by Cleveland family associates; IRS and FBI files list it as mob revenue source.

events.text: Opened during Prohibition as speakeasy.
Raided by U.S. Treasury agents.
Final closure after Kentucky reform election.

casinos.blurb: Long-running Newport casino and nightclub tied to Cleveland organized crime.

casinos.name: The 500 Club

mob.summary: Kefauver Committee and NJ Crime Commission document Philadelphia Mafia (Angelo Bruno family) control through owner Skinny D'Amato.

events.text: Opened as nightclub with illegal gambling by Skinny D'Amato on Boardwalk.
Kefauver Committee identifies 500 Club as Philadelphia Mafia gambling venue.
Demolished for Resorts Casino Hotel development.

casinos.blurb: Famous Boardwalk nightclub with illegal gambling 1930-73, documented Philadelphia Mafia (Bruno family) operation.

casinos.name: Railroad Pass Casino

mob.summary: Continuously operated since 1931; no credible organized crime allegations in regulatory records.

events.text: Opens shortly after Nevada legalizes gambling; oldest continuously operating casino in the state.
Major expansion adds hotel tower and modern gaming floor.

casinos.blurb: Nevada's oldest continuously operating casino, open since 1931 on the Las Vegas-Henderson border.

casinos.name: Club Harlem

mob.summary: No mob ownership documented in the sources checked.

events.text: Opened by Leroy 'Pop' Williams on Kentucky Avenue as premier Black nightclub with gambling.
NJ Crime Commission report alleges Philadelphia Mafia skim from gambling operations.
Closed after fire; building demolished 1992.

casinos.blurb: Legendary Kentucky Avenue nightclub 1935-86 with illegal gambling, alleged Philadelphia Mafia profit-sharing.

casinos.name: Colonial Inn

mob.summary: Frank Erickson and Chicago Outfit ran the Colonial Inn as a major wire-service hub and casino; documented in Kefauver Committee hearings and FBI files linking it to national bookmaking network.

events.text: Opens as restaurant and private club; illegal gambling and bookmaking begin almost immediately.
Kefauver Committee identifies Colonial Inn as key Florida node in Chicago Outfit's national wire service.
Florida Attorney General Richard Ervin secures permanent injunction closing the club after decades of raids.

casinos.blurb: The Colonial Inn served as South Florida's premier mob-run casino and the central wire-service relay for the Chicago Outfit's national bookmaking operation for over two decades.

casinos.name: Harold's Club

mob.summary: No documented or credible mob ties; family-owned throughout its history.

events.text: Harold Smith Sr. opens Harold's Club, famous for nationwide 'Harold's Club or Bust' billboards.
Club closes after 60 years; building later demolished for a parking garage.

casinos.blurb: Iconic family-run casino known for its massive outdoor advertising campaign across the American West.

casinos.name: Beverly Hills Club

mob.summary: Shondor Birns and Cleveland family held hidden interest; Kefauver Committee 1950 testimony confirmed mob control.

events.text: Opened as supper club with casino.
Featured in Kefauver Committee hearings.
Closed after federal tax eviction.

casinos.blurb: Newport's largest mob-run casino, centerpiece of the 'Little Las Vegas' strip on the Ohio River.

casinos.name: Harrah's Reno

mob.summary: No organised-crime control documented; founded by William F. Harrah.

events.text: Bill Harrah opens Harrah's Club, pioneering modern casino marketing.
Kefauver Committee hears testimony on organized crime ties to Reno gambling.

casinos.blurb: Flagship of the Harrah's empire, opened by Bill Harrah in 1937 and still operating on Virginia Street.

casinos.name: El Cortez Hotel & Casino

mob.summary: No documented mob ownership; operated by legitimate local investors from opening.

events.text: Opened as a downtown hotel and casino by Marion Hicks and J. Kell Houssels.
Added the 14-story Caballero Tower, becoming the tallest building in Las Vegas at the time.

casinos.blurb: Las Vegas's oldest continuously operating casino hotel, opened in 1941 on Fremont Street.

casinos.name: Balinese Room

mob.summary: The Maceo brothers ran gambling in Galveston for decades; the club was raided by the Texas Rangers in 1957.

events.text: Reopened as Balinese Room after renovation of Maceo's Club, featuring illegal casino gambling on pier over Gulf of Mexico.
Texas Rangers conduct surveillance documenting gambling operations for Governor Allan Shivers.
Rangers raid and permanently close the club; slot machines dumped into Gulf.

casinos.blurb: The Balinese Room was the flagship of the Maceo brothers' Galveston gambling empire, operating openly as a private club until a 1957 Texas Ranger raid ended its 15-year run.

casinos.name: Flamingo Las Vegas

mob.summary: Built with mob financing; Bugsy Siegel skimmed construction funds, leading to his 1947 murder; Lansky held hidden interests per FBI and Kefauver Committee findings.

events.text: Opened December 26 as the Strip's first luxury resort, financed by Bugsy Siegel and Meyer Lansky.
Bugsy Siegel murdered in Beverly Hills; mob associates took over operations.
Kirk Kerkorian purchased the property, ending direct mob-era ownership.

casinos.blurb: The Strip's first luxury resort, opened in 1946 with documented mob financing and the catalyst for modern Las Vegas.

casinos.name: Golden Nugget Las Vegas

mob.summary: Opened by Guy McAfee in 1946 and later run by Steve Wynn; no ownership by organised crime is documented in the sources checked.

events.text: Opened by Guy McAfee and partners as a luxury casino on Fremont Street.
Steve Wynn purchased a controlling interest, beginning his Las Vegas career.

casinos.blurb: Historic Fremont Street casino opened in 1946, later the launchpad for Steve Wynn's empire.

casinos.name: Mapes Hotel & Casino

mob.summary: No mob ownership documented in the sources checked.

events.text: Opens as Nevada's first high-rise hotel-casino, 12 stories tall.
Casino closes; hotel operates until 1986; building demolished in 2000 after years of vacancy.

casinos.blurb: Pioneering high-rise resort with documented Chicago Outfit backing, demolished in 2000 after decades of decline.

casinos.name: Desert Inn

mob.summary: Moe Dalitz, a Cleveland mob figure, was the public face; Kefauver Committee and Nevada Gaming Control Board documented hidden mob profit participation.

events.text: Opened April 24 by Moe Dalitz, Allard Roen, and Louis Goldman as a high-end Strip resort.
Steve Wynn purchased the Desert Inn, ending nearly four decades of Dalitz-family control.
Closed August 28; demolished in 2001 to make way for Wynn Las Vegas.

casinos.blurb: Moe Dalitz's flagship Strip resort from 1950 to 2000, with documented Cleveland mob ties throughout its early decades.

casinos.name: Sands Hotel and Casino

mob.summary: Kefauver Committee and FBI records confirm Chicago Outfit and Lansky hidden interests; skim operations documented in 1970s federal prosecutions.

events.text: Opened December 15 by Jake Freedman with mob-backed financing; became the Strip's premier entertainment venue.
Howard Hughes purchased the Sands, beginning corporate ownership.
Closed June 30 and imploded November 26 to make way for The Venetian.

casinos.blurb: Iconic 1952 Strip resort famous for the Copa Room and documented mob profit skimming until Hughes' 1967 purchase.

casinos.name: Carson Nugget

mob.summary: Family-owned throughout; clean regulatory history per Nevada Gaming Control Board.

events.text: Opens as Carson City's first major casino on North Carson Street.
Adds 140-room hotel tower and expands gaming space significantly.

casinos.blurb: Capital city landmark casino, family-operated since 1954 with major 2000s expansion.

casinos.name: Dunes Hotel & Casino

mob.summary: Reporting and Nevada licensing files tied hidden interests in the early years to organised crime.

casinos.blurb: Strip landmark with an Arabian theme, imploded in 1993.

casinos.name: Riviera Casino

mob.summary: Credible reporting links early investors to Midwest mob figures, but no convictions tied directly to casino operations.

events.text: Opened April 20 as the first high-rise on the Strip, financed by a group including Gus Greenbaum.
Meshulam Riklis purchased a controlling interest, beginning a turbulent corporate era.
Closed May 4; demolished in 2016 for the Las Vegas Convention Center expansion.

casinos.blurb: First high-rise Strip resort (1955), operated for 60 years before demolition for convention center expansion.

casinos.name: Fremont Hotel & Casino

mob.summary: Part of the Argent Corporation group skimmed in the 1970s; the Strawman case brought convictions.

casinos.blurb: Downtown tower that opened in 1956.

casinos.name: Tropicana Las Vegas

mob.summary: Hidden mob interests at opening (Frank Costello); in the 1970s Kansas City mob figures skimmed the casino in the FBI investigation known as Operation Strawman.

events.text: Opened April 4 as 'Tropicana Resort & Casino' with a South Seas theme.
Ramada Inns purchased the property, bringing corporate management.
Closed April 2; slated for demolition to build a baseball stadium for the Athletics.

casinos.blurb: Tropical-themed Strip resort opened in 1957, closed in 2024 after 67 years for a planned ballpark.

casinos.name: Stardust Resort & Casino

mob.summary: Skimmed for years: the 1970s-80s FBI case Operation Strawman and the Argent Corporation scandal ended in convictions; the story behind the film Casino.

casinos.blurb: Biggest skim of the Strip era.

casinos.name: Caesars Palace

mob.summary: Construction financed by Teamsters pension fund under mob influence per federal convictions; no direct mob ownership after opening.

events.text: Opened August 5 by Jay Sarno with Teamsters pension fund financing.
Hosted the first major boxing 'superfight' (Ali vs. Foreman was 1974; correction: hosted numerous historic bouts).
Reopened after extensive renovation following 2018 sale to Vici Properties and lease to Caesars Entertainment.

casinos.blurb: Roman-themed mega-resort opened in 1966 with Teamsters pension financing later tied to mob influence.

casinos.name: Riverside Resort

mob.summary: Founded by Don Laughlin; no credible allegations of organized crime involvement.

events.text: Don Laughlin opens the first casino in what becomes Laughlin, Nevada.
Town of Laughlin incorporates, named after the founder.

casinos.blurb: Don Laughlin's original casino sparked the development of the entire Laughlin gaming corridor on the Colorado River.

casinos.name: Circus Circus Las Vegas

mob.summary: Jay Sarno's financing connections raised regulatory scrutiny; no proven mob ownership after licensing.

events.text: Opened October 18 by Jay Sarno and Stanley Mallin as a family-oriented circus-themed resort.
Sold to William Bennett and William Pennington, beginning decades of family ownership.
Sold to Phil Ruffin; operated by MGM Resorts under lease.

casinos.blurb: Circus-themed family resort opened in 1968, long owned by the Bennett family before 2019 sale.

casinos.name: Resorts Casino Hotel

mob.summary: Resorts International grew out of the Mary Carter Paint Company, which press and investigators linked to Lansky associates in the 1960s.

events.text: Opened as first legal casino outside Nevada on May 26.
NJ Casino Control Commission fines Resorts $200,000 for regulatory violations.

casinos.blurb: First legal casino in Atlantic City, opened 1978 by James Crosby's Archway Investments.

casinos.name: Bally's Atlantic City

mob.summary: No documented or credible alleged mob ties found in NJ Casino Control Commission licensing records.

events.text: Opened as Bally's Park Place on December 30 by Bally Manufacturing.
Rebranded from Bally's to Bally's Atlantic City after Twin River Worldwide Holdings acquisition.

casinos.blurb: Third Atlantic City casino, opened 1979 by Bally Manufacturing with no mob ties in licensing record.

casinos.name: Caesars Atlantic City

mob.summary: Alleged Chicago Outfit ties via Teamsters pension fund financing investigated by FBI and NJCCC in 1979-80.

events.text: Opened as Boardwalk Regency on June 26, financed partly by Teamsters Central States Pension Fund.
Renamed Caesars Atlantic City after Caesars World acquisition.

casinos.blurb: Second Atlantic City casino, opened 1979 with Teamsters pension financing later scrutinized for mob links.

casinos.name: Harrah's Atlantic City

mob.summary: No documented or credible alleged mob ties; developed by Holiday Inns Inc. with clean NJCCC licensing.

events.text: Opened August 13 as first Marina District casino by Holiday Inns Inc.
Acquired by Caesars Entertainment in Harrah's Entertainment merger.

casinos.blurb: First Marina District casino, opened 1980 by Holiday Inns with clean regulatory record.

casinos.name: Tropicana Atlantic City

mob.summary: No documented or credible alleged mob ties; developed by Ramada Inns with clean NJCCC licensing.

events.text: Opened November 23 as Tropicana Casino & Resort by Ramada Inns.
Sold to Aztar Corporation after Ramada restructuring.

casinos.blurb: Opened 1981 by Ramada Inns, later Aztar and Caesars Entertainment property with no mob ties.

casinos.name: Trump Plaza Hotel and Casino

mob.summary: Reporting linked concrete and construction contractors on Trump projects to organised crime; no casino ownership by the mob is established.

events.text: Opened May 14 as Trump Plaza Hotel & Casino, developed by Donald Trump.
NJCCC fines Trump Plaza $75,000 for employing unlicensed contractors with alleged mob ties.
Closed permanently September 16 after bankruptcy.

casinos.blurb: Trump's first Atlantic City casino, opened 1984, closed 2014; fined for contractor mob ties.

casinos.name: Canterbury Park

mob.summary: Operated as a licensed horse racing track and card room with no organized crime ties.

events.text: Opened for live thoroughbred and quarter horse racing in 1985; card room added in 2000 after legislative approval.

casinos.blurb: Canterbury Park is Minnesota's only thoroughbred and quarter horse racing venue, which added a licensed card room in 2000 to become a racino.

casinos.name: Colorado Belle

mob.summary: Developed by local investors; no documented or alleged mob connections.

events.text: Opens as a replica 1800s paddlewheel riverboat casino on the Colorado River.
Temporarily closed during COVID-19 pandemic; reopened in 2022 under new ownership.

casinos.blurb: Distinctive riverboat-themed casino that became a Laughlin landmark since its 1980 opening.

casinos.name: Trump Taj Mahal Casino Resort

mob.summary: Reporting linked concrete and construction contractors on Trump projects to organised crime; no casino ownership by the mob is established.

events.text: Opened April 4 as world's largest casino; financed with junk bonds.
Fined $477,000 by NJCCC for Currency Transaction Reporting violations; mob ties documented in commission report.
Closed October 10 after labor dispute and bankruptcy.

casinos.blurb: Opened 1990, NJCCC documented Philadelphia Mafia and Genovese ties; closed 2016, reopened 2018 as Hard Rock.

casinos.name: Grand Casino Mille Lacs

mob.summary: Owned and operated by the Mille Lacs Band of Ojibwe with no organized crime involvement.

events.text: Opened as the second tribal casino in Minnesota under a state compact with the Mille Lacs Band of Ojibwe.

casinos.blurb: Grand Casino Mille Lacs, opened in 1991 by the Mille Lacs Band of Ojibwe, was Minnesota's second tribal casino and a major economic driver for the region.

casinos.name: Casino Magic

events.text: Opened as a riverboat casino in Biloxi.
Destroyed by Hurricane Katrina and never reopened.

casinos.blurb: Casino Magic operated as a riverboat casino in Biloxi from 1993 until Hurricane Katrina destroyed it in 2005.

casinos.name: Foxwoods Resort Casino

mob.summary: Owned and operated by the Mashantucket Pequot Tribal Nation with no organized crime involvement.

events.text: Opened as a high-stakes bingo hall in 1986; expanded to table games in 1992 and slot machines in 1993 under a state compact.

casinos.blurb: Foxwoods Resort Casino, operated by the Mashantucket Pequot Tribal Nation, grew from a 1986 bingo hall into one of the world's largest casino resorts.

casinos.name: Mystic Lake Casino Hotel

mob.summary: Owned and operated by the Shakopee Mdewakanton Sioux Community with no organized crime involvement.

events.text: Opened as a bingo hall in 1988 and expanded into a full casino in 1992 under the Indian Gaming Regulatory Act.

casinos.blurb: Mystic Lake Casino Hotel, owned by the Shakopee Mdewakanton Sioux Community, became one of the largest and most successful tribal casinos in the Upper Midwest after its 1992 expansion.

casinos.name: President Casino Broadwater Resort

events.text: Opened as a riverboat casino in Biloxi.
Closed after Hurricane Katrina damage.

casinos.blurb: President Casino Broadwater Resort operated in Biloxi from 1992 until Hurricane Katrina.

casinos.name: Casino Queen

mob.summary: Riverboat casino on the Mississippi River.

events.text: Opened as Casino Queen riverboat.
Expanded with land-based facilities.

casinos.blurb: The only casino in the Metro East, operating on the Mississippi River since 1993.

casinos.name: Harrah's Joliet

mob.summary: Licensed riverboat casino operated by Caesars Entertainment.

events.text: Opened as Harrah's Joliet riverboat casino.
Converted to land-based casino after state law change.

casinos.blurb: A major Joliet riverboat casino that transitioned to a land-based facility in 2018.

casinos.name: Hollywood Casino Aurora

mob.summary: No documented mob ties; licensed riverboat casino.

events.text: Opened as Aurora's first riverboat casino.
Renovated and expanded to land-based facility.

casinos.blurb: Illinois' first riverboat casino in Aurora, originally a paddlewheel boat now a land-based resort.

casinos.name: Turning Stone Resort Casino

mob.summary: Owned and operated by the Oneida Indian Nation with no organized crime involvement.

events.text: Opened as a bingo hall in 1993 and expanded to table games and slots after a 2001 compact with New York State.

casinos.blurb: Turning Stone Resort Casino, operated by the Oneida Indian Nation, opened in 1993 and became a major destination resort in upstate New York.

casinos.name: Boomtown Casino

events.text: Opened as a riverboat casino in Harvey, Louisiana.

casinos.blurb: Boomtown Casino in Harvey has operated continuously since 1994 as a riverboat casino on the Mississippi River.

casinos.name: Grand Victoria Casino Elgin

mob.summary: Licensed riverboat casino on the Fox River.

events.text: Opened as Grand Victoria Casino Elgin.
Converted to land-based casino.

casinos.blurb: A Fox River riverboat casino that became a land-based resort in 2019.

casinos.name: Treasure Chest Casino

events.text: Opened as a riverboat casino in Kenner, Louisiana.

casinos.blurb: Treasure Chest Casino in Kenner has been a staple of Jefferson Parish gaming since 1994.

casinos.name: Mohegan Sun

mob.summary: Owned and operated by the Mohegan Tribe with no organized crime involvement.

events.text: Opened on October 12, 1996, as the second major tribal casino in Connecticut under a compact with the state.

casinos.blurb: Mohegan Sun, opened in 1996 by the Mohegan Tribe, became one of the largest casino resorts in the United States.

casinos.name: IP Casino Resort Spa

events.text: Opened as the Imperial Palace casino resort in Biloxi.

casinos.blurb: IP Casino Resort Spa has operated in Biloxi since 1997, originally as the Imperial Palace.

casinos.name: Bellagio

mob.summary: Developed by Steve Wynn's Mirage Resorts with no mob ties; fully corporate financing.

events.text: Opened October 15 on the former Dunes site, costing $1.6 billion, a record at the time.
Mirage Resorts acquired by MGM Grand Inc., forming MGM Mirage.

casinos.blurb: Steve Wynn's $1.6 billion luxury resort opened in 1998, famous for its fountains and art collection.

casinos.name: Beau Rivage Resort & Casino

events.text: Opened as a luxury resort casino on the Biloxi beachfront.

casinos.blurb: Beau Rivage is a luxury resort casino on the Biloxi beachfront, opened in 1999.

casinos.name: Harrah's New Orleans

events.text: Opened as a riverboat casino on the Mississippi River.
Converted to a land-based casino after Hurricane Katrina.

casinos.blurb: Harrah's New Orleans is the only land-based casino in downtown New Orleans, operating since 1999.

casinos.name: MGM Grand Detroit

mob.summary: Opened by MGM Resorts International as a licensed commercial casino with no organized crime ties.

events.text: Opened as one of three licensed commercial casinos in Detroit following the 1996 voter referendum.

casinos.blurb: MGM Grand Detroit is a major commercial casino resort that opened in 1999 as part of Detroit's legalized gaming market.

casinos.name: MotorCity Casino Hotel

mob.summary: Developed by Marian Ilitch and opened as a licensed commercial casino with no organized crime ties.

events.text: Opened as Detroit's first permanent commercial casino after Michigan voters approved Proposal E in 1996.

casinos.blurb: MotorCity Casino Hotel is a locally owned commercial casino resort that opened in 1999 following the legalization of casino gambling in Detroit.

casinos.name: Greektown Casino-Hotel

mob.summary: Opened as a licensed commercial casino by the Sault Ste. Marie Tribe of Chippewa Indians and later sold to Penn Entertainment with no organized crime ties.

events.text: Opened as Detroit's third commercial casino in the historic Greektown district.

casinos.blurb: Greektown Casino-Hotel opened in 2000 as Detroit's third licensed commercial casino in the city's historic Greektown neighborhood.

casinos.name: Pechanga Resort Casino

mob.summary: Owned and operated by the Pechanga Band of Luiseño Indians with no organized crime involvement.

events.text: Opened on June 24, 2002, after the Pechanga Band of Luiseño Indians signed a gaming compact with California.

casinos.blurb: Pechanga Resort Casino, opened in 2002 by the Pechanga Band of Luiseño Indians, is one of the largest casino resorts on the West Coast.

casinos.name: Borgata Hotel Casino & Spa

mob.summary: No documented or credible alleged mob ties; developed by Boyd Gaming and MGM Mirage with clean NJCCC licensing.

events.text: Opened July 3 as joint venture of Boyd Gaming and MGM Mirage.
MGM Resorts acquires Boyd Gaming's stake for full ownership.

casinos.blurb: Opened 2003 as Boyd/MGM joint venture in Marina District with no mob ties in licensing record.

casinos.name: Hard Rock Hotel & Casino Biloxi

events.text: Opened as a music-themed resort casino in Biloxi.

casinos.blurb: Hard Rock Biloxi brings music-themed gaming to the Mississippi Gulf Coast.

casinos.name: Golden Nugget Biloxi

mob.summary: Opened by Guy McAfee in 1946 and later run by Steve Wynn; no ownership by organised crime is documented in the sources checked.

events.text: Opened as a Landry's-owned resort casino in Biloxi.

casinos.blurb: Golden Nugget Biloxi is a Landry's-owned casino resort opened in 2012.

timeline.text: El Cortez opens in downtown Las Vegas; the Strip era is about to begin.
The Flamingo opens on 26 December, financed by organised-crime figures and Bugsy Siegel.
Bugsy Siegel is shot dead at his Beverly Hills home.
The Kefauver Committee begins hearings on organised crime in interstate commerce, including gambling.
The Kefauver Committee publishes its findings on organised crime and illegal gambling.
Nevada creates the Gaming Control Board to license and police casinos.
Police raid the Apalachin, New York, meeting of mob leaders.
Nevada starts its list of excluded persons, the "Black Book".
Newport and Covington, Kentucky, end their wide-open gambling.
Howard Hughes buys the Desert Inn, starting corporate ownership on the Strip.
Nevada passes the Corporate Gaming Act, letting public companies hold casino licences.
New Jersey voters approve casino gambling limited to Atlantic City.
Resorts International opens the first legal casino in Atlantic City on 26 May.
Mob enforcer Tony Spilotro is murdered; the Strawman skimming cases bring convictions.
The Indian Gaming Regulatory Act creates the legal frame for tribal casinos.
Foxwoods opens in Connecticut, the first of the big tribal casinos.
The Supreme Court strikes down the federal ban on state-licensed sports betting.
